title: What is Transfer Learning?
description: How knowledge learned on one task speeds up another: reusing expert-trained pre-trained models and fine-tuning them when labeled data or compute are scarce.
content:
**Transfer learning** is a concept in machine learning where the knowledge gained from training a model on one task is applied to a different but related one. Instead of starting the learning process from scratch, we leverage a pre-trained model architecture on a new dataset.

Transfer learning is especially useful when:
• The new task has limited labeled data
• Computational resources are scarce

In both cases it allows for faster convergence of the learning process.

**Pre-trained models** are pre-built models that are trained on a vast amount of data by experts and are able to be reused. They have already learned to recognize patterns and generalize them within the knowledge they were trained on, so they can be fine-tuned or adapted to specific tasks or datasets with relatively little additional training data.

**Fine-tuning** is the process of taking pre-trained models and adjusting their parameters - typically the weights of some of their layers, sometimes hyperparameters - in order to adapt them to a new, specific task.

By fine-tuning, we allow the model to adapt to the nuances and characteristics of the new dataset while retaining valuable information from the pre-training dataset.

In short: pre-trained models carry general knowledge learned from a large dataset, and fine-tuning reshapes that knowledge for a specific task - so the model does not have to learn everything from zero.
